# wellbeing_employee_roster (Resource)

Manages the company's entire employee roster.

The Wellbeing API has no per-employee endpoint: `PUT /Employee` replaces the whole set, and employees absent from the payload are deleted. This resource therefore owns every employee created through the API, and there is deliberately no `wellbeing_employee` resource.

~> **Destroying this resource does not delete anyone.** Terraform forgets the roster and leaves Wellbeing untouched. Use `terraform import` to adopt an existing roster back into state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The Wellbeing API replaces the whole roster on every write, so this single
# resource owns every employee created through the API. Employees omitted here
# are deleted by the API on the next apply.
resource "wellbeing_employee_roster" "this" {
  # Refuse to apply a change touching a quarter or more of the roster. Matches
  # the batch limit configured for the company in the Wellbeing portal.
  batch_limit_percent = 25

  employee = {
    for employee in local.hr_export : employee.staff_number => {
      firstname         = employee.first_name
      lastname          = employee.last_name
      email             = employee.email
      employment_status = employee.on_leave ? "on_leave" : "active"
      gender            = employee.gender
      phone_number      = employee.mobile

      dimensions = {
        Department       = employee.department
        ImmediateManager = employee.manager_name
        Location         = employee.office
      }
    }
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "60m"
    update = "60m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `employee` (Attributes Map) The complete set of employees, keyed by your internal `EmployeeID`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--employee))

### Optional

- `batch_limit_percent` (Number) Optional plan-time guard mirroring the company's configured batch limit. When set, an apply that would change more than this percentage of the roster fails before any request is sent. The API applies the same rule server-side but does not expose the configured value, and a rejected import may only surface after a long queued wait. The check is skipped when the company has fewer than 100 employees, matching the API.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The company ID this roster belongs to.

<a id="nestedatt--employee"></a>
### Nested Schema for `employee`

Required:

- `email` (String) E-mail address. Must be unique across the company.
- `employment_status` (String) Employment status. One of `active` or `on_leave`.
- `firstname` (String) First name of the employee.
- `lastname` (String) Last name of the employee.

Optional:

- `dimensions` (Map of String) Reporting dimensions such as `Department`, `Role`, `ImmediateManager`, `Location` or `Division`. The API accepts the first three as dedicated fields and returns all of them nested here; the provider handles that difference, so configure everything through this map.
- `gender` (String) Gender. One of `female`, `male` or `unknown`.
- `invitation_date` (String) When to send the invitation, formatted `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`. Applies only to employees being created; the API never returns it, so the configured value is carried forward in state unchanged.
- `job_title` (String) Role in the company, for example `Sales Manager`.
- `phone_number` (String) Cell phone in international format, for example `+4523232323`. Must be unique.

Read-Only:

- `company_id` (Number) Company the employee belongs to.
- `external_id` (String) External ID recorded by Wellbeing.
- `first_invitation_date` (String) When the first invitation was sent.
- `fullname` (String) Full name as assembled by Wellbeing.
- `id` (Number) Wellbeing's internal numeric employee ID.
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the employee's account is locked.
- `opt_out` (Boolean) Whether the employee has opted out of surveys.
- `sourced_from_external_system` (Boolean) Whether Wellbeing considers this employee externally sourced.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the company ID.
terraform import wellbeing_employee_roster.this 1000
```
